topics.label: Course overview and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students and outlines the lecture goals, structure, and expected learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: endogenous mechanisms, environmental exposures, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental concepts of cancer development by exploring the balance between endogenous mutational processes, bad luck, genetic background, and epidemiological evidence for environmental causes.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections contribute to malignancy, illustrated by the detailed etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens: mechanisms of initiation, promotion, and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore diverse environmental carcinogens, explaining how metabolic activation, direct DNA damage, chronic inflammation, tumor promotion, and developmental tissue states drive carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the laboratory, genomic, and epidemiological approaches used to detect mutational signatures and evaluate the carcinogenicity of substances.

topics.label: Carcinogenic risk assessment and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes by evaluating real-world risk-benefit tradeoffs of carcinogen exposure and summarizing the main themes of the lecture.
